message.reasoning:
I'm planning a comprehensive JUnit 4 test suite for jsoup's Element class, mapping out test methods for constructor validation, tag name handling, block detection, id/attribute access, dataset, and parent/ancestor traversal to cover the key branches and edge cases. I continue outlining the remaining test methods: child and children access including out-of-bounds cases, text/data node retrieval, CSS selection, child insertion methods (append/prepend/insert) with null and boundary checks, wrapping, CSS selector generation, and sibling navigation (next/previous/first/last element sibling, sibling index) covering both null-parent and populated-parent scenarios, finishing with getElementsByTag and getElementById edge cases. Then I list the full suite of attribute-based and index-based element selectors (by class, attribute presence, value matching with starting/ending/containing/not, regex pattern matching with valid and invalid patterns, index comparisons), text-matching selectors for both full and own text, and getAllElements, followed by text extraction behaviors (combined text, block elements, br handling, own text, hasText, data), className and classNames retrieval including set-based variants, and class membership checks with case insensitivity. Continuing the method list: addClass, removeClass, toggleClass with containment checks, val() differentiating textarea from other inputs, html() getter and setter, toString, equals with same/null/different-class/different-instance cases, hashCode, and clone. Given how large this class is, I'm planning to write thorough tests leveraging Jsoup.parse for convenience alongside direct Element construction where needed, and now I'm working out the necessary imports for parsing, nodes, selectors, and JUnit assertions before starting the test class itself. Since this is testing jsoup's own source as part of the Defects4J benchmark, Jsoup.parse and related classes are part of the codebase under test, so I can freely use them rather than treating them as external dependencies. Now I'm sketching out concrete test method names covering the constructor, tag name handling, block detection, id presence, attribute chaining, dataset, and parent/ancestor traversal. Continuing to list test method names, now covering children filtering, text/data nodes, select, and the various append/prepend/insert child and HTML/text manipulation methods with their null-check and bounds-check variants. Continuing to list test cases... Still listing test method names... I'll use Jsoup's parsing utilities to build test elements easily. For insertChildren edge cases, I'm working through the negative index logic—for an element with two children, inserting at index -1 should land at the end, while an out-of-bounds positive index like 5 should trigger an IllegalArgumentException. I'm assuming Validate.isTrue and Validate.notNull both throw IllegalArgumentException, since that's the typical jsoup pattern, though I'll note this assumption is uncertain. Now moving on to coding the cssSelector nth-child branch. For the nth-child test, I need two sibling elements with the same tag so the parent's selector match count exceeds one, triggering the nth-child logic — like two sibling `

` tags inside a `

`. For the id case, I'll set an id attribute and confirm the selector resolves to "#id". For the Document-parent case, I need to parse full HTML and check that the top-level child under Document returns a plain selector without the usual " > " parent prefix. I can simplify this by parsing `` and grabbing the first child, then asserting its selector is just "html" since its parent is a Document rather than another element. For the parentless case, I'll build a standalone div element with no attributes and confirm its selector is simply "div". Then I'll test the id branch by setting an id attribute and verifying the selector becomes "#foo", and move on to testing classes next. Writing remaining test cases... For the matching methods I need to test both valid and invalid regex patterns since there's a try/catch for PatternSyntaxException. I should also cover toggleClass, hasClass case variations, val() for textareas versus other elements, hasText for blank versus non-blank nodes, data() extraction, and text() spacing around block elements and br tags. For equals(), I need to verify same instance returns true, null and different classes return false, and distinct instances with identical content still return false since the implementation explicitly checks "this==o" after the superclass check. I'll test two freshly constructed Elements with identical tags and attributes but different instances to confirm they're not equal. For hashCode, I'll just check consistency across repeated calls rather than assuming specific values. For clone(), this reveals an interesting bug: cloned elements will never be equal to their source since equals only checks reference identity, which looks like the actual defect this Jsoup bug is centered on. I also want to verify Validate's exception behavior, expecting IllegalArgumentException for notNull/notEmpty/isTrue checks, though I'll note these assumptions in comments since the exact implementation could differ slightly. I'll also write tests for insertChildren with out-of-bounds indices and appendChild with null arguments, expecting validation failures in both cases. Looking at firstElementSibling(), I notice it calls parent().children() without a null-check on parent(), so if there's no parent this would throw a NullPointerException rather than returning gracefully. This differs from nextElementSibling/previousElementSibling which guard against null parentNode, and from elementSiblingIndex() which explicitly returns 0 when parent() is null. I should write a test confirming firstElementSibling() and lastElementSibling() both NPE when called on a standalone element with no parent -- this is a real behavioral quirk worth catching. I'm also planning a test where a parent has two child elements: calling firstElementSibling() on either child returns the first child in the sibling list, since the method just returns siblings.get(0) regardless of which element invoked it. I'll write lastElementSibling() tests following the same pattern. Next I need to test nextElementSibling/previousElementSibling when parentNode is null (returns null) and at the boundary indices when there is a parent. Then for accumulateParents/parents(), I need to check that a standalone element with no parent returns empty Elements, and figure out what "#root" tagName check actually refers to—likely a special pseudo-root node used internally rather than the Document's own nodeName. Actually, I recall jsoup's Document is constructed with Tag.valueOf("#root"), so parents() naturally stops before including the document itself. That means for a nested structure like div > p parsed from a fragment, calling parents() on the p element should return just [div, body, html], excluding the root document node—I should verify this with a quick parse test. Now I want to also verify the text() method's block-spacing logic, which inserts a space before block elements or br tags if the accumulated text doesn't already end in whitespace—testing this requires a structure like a paragraph containing inline text followed by a nested div. That confirms the br test case works with "Hello World" as expected. Now I'm checking ownText() behavior, which only adds whitespace for literal "br" tags rather than any block element, and doesn't recurse into child elements like div -- so nested text inside a div wouldn't get included at all in ownText(). I realize the predictable example is actually the javadoc's own case: parsing "

Hello there now!

" should give ownText "Hello now!" since the trailing text node " now!" retains its leading space. I should write a test using this exact source to verify that expected output. Now I'm thinking through hasText(): blank whitespace-only elements should return false, elements with direct text should return true, and elements with nested text (recursively) should also return true, while nested blank elements should return false. I'll write tests covering each of these branches—plain text, nested with content, and nested with only whitespace—to exercise both the loop and the recursive call in hasText(). For data(), I'm testing an element with a script tag containing a data node plus a nested element with its own script, verifying that both the direct DataNode branch and the recursive Element branch of data() correctly aggregate the script contents. Then for className()/classNames(), I'm checking that a fresh element with no class attribute returns an empty string and empty set, and after setting class="a b c", className() returns the full string while classNames() returns a set of three distinct names. Now I'm testing the classNames(Set) setter to confirm it rebuilds the class attribute from a LinkedHashSet, then verifying hasClass() works case-insensitively, and testing addClass, removeClass, and toggleClass behavior for adding, removing, and flipping class membership on a div. I'm checking that val() returns the value attribute for input elements but the text content for textarea elements, and that val(value) correctly sets the value attribute for inputs while setting text for textareas. Then I test html() getting and setting inner HTML on a div, noting I may need a contains check since pretty-printing could add extra whitespace or newlines. I also verify toString() matches outerHtml(), and test equals()/hashCode() behavior confirming Element uses identity-based equality -- an element equals itself but not null, a different type, or another separately created element with identical content. For clone(), I check it produces a distinct object that's still not equal to the original under this identity-based rule, documenting that quirk. Then I plan to assemble the full test code with proper imports, including Validate exception checks, making sure it's syntactically coherent even though I can't execute it. I'm also covering null/empty-argument validation tests across the API: constructor rejecting null tag, tagName rejecting empty strings, appendChild/prependChild/append/prepend rejecting null nodes, insertChildren rejecting null or out-of-bounds indices, and the various getElementBy* selector methods rejecting empty strings. Beyond that, I'm checking classNames/addClass/removeClass/toggleClass and text() reject null input, plus confirming invalid regex patterns passed to attribute-matching and text-matching methods throw IllegalArgumentException. Now I'm putting together the final Java test file using Jsoup.parse with some shared helper assertions. I also want to verify Tag.valueOf accepts arbitrary unknown tag names without throwing, and I'm checking prependChild/prependElement/appendElement/appendText/prependText behave as expected along with before/after insertion producing the correct sibling structure in the parsed document. Still verifying children order and asserting positions match expected nodes, then moving on to test wrap() behavior, making sure the element has text and proper structure before wrapping. I decide to test wrap using a realistic parsed document instead: parse a div containing a paragraph, select it, call wrap with a section tag, and confirm the paragraph's parent is now "section." That seems like a well-grounded test based on documented behavior, so I'll move forward with writing the full test suite now. Given how many methods need coverage, I'll present everything as one complete test class and follow it with a summary table grouped by method area rather than listing every individual assertion, to keep things readable.
